stem:
Which part of the sentence has an error? If the sentence is correct, choose "No error".

The officer whom answered the phone gave me the wrong form.
hints: "Who" and "whom" are not the same. One is for the doer of an action, the other for the receiver.
Look at the words "___ answered the phone". Who did the answering? Try putting "he" or "him" in the blank.
Swap test: if "he" fits, use "who". If "him" fits, use "whom". Do the test, then check the other parts.

steps.action: Find "whom" and the words after it: "whom answered the phone".
Swap in he or him: "he answered the phone" sounds right; "him answered the phone" sounds wrong.
steps.why: "Who" works like "he": the doer. "Whom" works like "him": the receiver. Both "him" and "whom" end in -m.

steps.action: "He" fits, so the word must be "who": "The officer who answered the phone".
Check the other parts. "answered the phone" and "gave me the wrong form" are correct.
steps.why: "Me" is right after "gave", because the form was given to me.

steps.action: The error is "The officer whom". It should be "The officer who".

trapNotes.answered the phone: This part is correct. "Answered" is in the past tense, which matches "gave".
trapNotes.gave me the wrong form: "Me" is correct here because it receives the action of "gave". "Gave I" would be wrong.
trapNotes.No error: "Whom" sounds more formal, so it may look correct. But the officer is the one who answered, the doer, so "who" is needed.
